title: Window Tool Panel with Recursive Category Groups
description:
All windows must have a tool panel on the bottom left. Tool node groups (e.g. selection) act as categories. When a group tool node is activated, the panel expands with another line. This works recursively. There can only be one active group per level (at most one active per level; zero active collapses that line).

Implementation per approved plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/ui-all-windows-must-cheerful-llama.md:
1. Render the bottom-left toolbar overlay + WindowToolbarChrome unconditionally on every Window (ui/js/react/index.tsx), with a disabled unfold toggle when there are no tools.
2. Add groupToolNodesByCategory in framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx to synthesize category collections (selection/tools/actions/history/sync) from a window's top-level tool nodes, matching wgpu's partition_tools_by_category ordering; wire into windowToolbarNode.
3. Rewrite buildToolbarRibbonSegments/reconcileToolPath so collections never auto-activate: at most one active group per level, zero active collapses the line, no leaf-only-sibling flattening, no single-collection auto-drill. Update ToolTree's picker onValueChange so re-clicking the active toggle collapses that line and deeper lines.
4. Add "tools"/"sync" to UiToolbarParentCategory i18n plus De/En entries; extend resolveControlLabelId to resolve window-scoped ui.toolbar.<windowId>.group.<slug> ids.
5. Sweep plugin tools()/mode_tools Rust implementations (writer, cad, s, sequence, procedural, draw, note, trinity, layout, shooting, process, lowpoly) to tag top-level tool nodes with explicit .with_category(...).
6. Extend existing tests (framework/renderer/react/index.test.ts toolbar-ribbon describe, ui/js/react index.tsx i18n test) and existing stories (.storybook/stories/ui/Toolbar.stories.tsx, Window.stories.tsx) — no new files.
summary: Fixed three bugs reported after the initial tool-panel implementation, all in framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx: (1) Doubling — a category bucket containing exactly one already-meaningful collection (e.g. lowpoly's/draw's own "Selection" collection) is now reused directly instead of being re-wrapped in a synthetic category collection with a duplicate-looking label; groupToolNodesByCategory reassigns only its `order`. (2) Actions no longer shown per-window — windowToolbarNode now groups tools with an explicit allowlist (new WINDOW_TOOL_CATEGORIES = ["selection", "tools"]), since only selection/tools are genuinely window-scoped. (3) History (and Actions) moved to the shared footer — traced that mode-wide tools declared via .mode_tools() (e.g. s-play's history collection) were attached identically to every window kind by the existing render loop, so showing them per-window duplicated the same chip across every window pane in a mode. Added dedupeToolNodesById (dedupe by id across all windows' tool lists) and a footerModeToolTree computed via groupToolNodesByCategory(deduped, FOOTER_TOOL_CATEGORIES = ["actions", "history"]), rendered inline in the pre-existing app-level Footer alongside the sync card. groupToolNodesByCategory's signature changed to accept a `categories` allowlist param (default: all 5) to support this window/footer split. Extended framework/renderer/react/index.test.ts with new coverage (singleton-collection reuse, multi-node still wraps, category scoping via the allowlist param, dedupeToolNodesById); all 93 tests pass. Updated .storybook/stories/ui/Toolbar.stories.tsx (renamed the window demo to selection/tools only, added a new "Footer: Mode-Wide Categories" story with direction="inline") and Window.stories.tsx (removed Actions from the window toolbar demo tree) so the docs no longer model the now-fixed incorrect pattern. Verified via cargo build/tests only affect Rust files, which were untouched this round; ui/js/react vitest still shows the same 218/224 passing with the same 6 pre-existing unrelated failures. Storybook visual verification was attempted again but blocked by the same Browser-pane/CDP connectivity issue as the prior session (server itself confirmed healthy via curl); relying on the passing unit/component test suite instead.
